title.en: The human heart, circulation and blood pressure

text.en: Your heart is about the size of your fist and beats 72 to 75 times a minute for your whole life. Each beat has a precise sequence.

Circulation may be open, with blood in sinuses and no capillaries (arthropods, molluscs), or closed, with blood always inside vessels (vertebrates); William Harvey discovered the closed system in 1628.
The human heart is a four-chambered muscular organ enclosed in the pericardium: two thin-walled atria above and two thick-walled ventricles below; the left ventricle wall is about three times thicker than the right.
The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the vena cavae and coronary sinus; the left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins.
Tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and ventricle, the bicuspid (mitral) valve between the left atrium and ventricle, and semilunar valves guard the pulmonary artery and aorta.
Systemic circulation carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the body; pulmonary circulation carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs; coronary circulation feeds the heart muscle.
Because blood passes twice through the heart in one round, human circulation is double circulation, and oxygenated and deoxygenated blood do not mix.
The SA node in the right atrium is the pacemaker; the impulse goes to the AV node, the bundle of His and the Purkinje fibres, so the heart beat is myogenic.
The cardiac cycle lasts 0.8 s: atrial systole 0.1 s, ventricular systole 0.3 s and ventricular diastole 0.4 s.
Heart sounds: lubb from closing of tricuspid and bicuspid valves, dupp from closing of semilunar valves.
Blood pressure is 120 mm Hg systolic over 80 mm Hg diastolic in a healthy adult; it is measured with a sphygmomanometer and the heart is listened to with a stethoscope.
Pulse rate is normally 70 to 90 per minute; sustained high pressure is hypertension and low pressure is hypotension.

problem.en: Trace a drop of blood from the right atrium to the lungs and back to the left atrium.

text.en: Right atrium to right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.
Right ventricle to the lungs through the pulmonary artery.
Lungs to the left atrium through the pulmonary veins.

prompt.en: Explain the cardiac cycle and the origin of the heart sounds.

requiredIdeas.en: Atrial systole 0.1 s, ventricular systole 0.3 s, diastole 0.4 s

points.en: Four chambers; tricuspid on the right, bicuspid on the left.
Systemic, pulmonary and coronary circulations; double circulation in humans.
SA node is the pacemaker; one cycle lasts 0.8 s.
Normal BP 120/80 mm Hg; sphygmomanometer measures it.
